statement: This repository analyzes single-epoch stellar radial velocities from the DESI DR1 Milky Way stellar catalogue, not the extragalactic BAO catalogue used for DESI cosmology.
limitations: The same instrument supports several surveys, so instrument context alone does not identify which scientific sample a result uses.

statement: DESI constrains cosmic expansion and dark-energy models with extragalactic BAO tracers, but this stellar radial-velocity audit does not estimate a cosmological parameter or test dark energy.
limitations: Calibration quality can matter broadly to survey science, but that indirect relevance is not a dark-energy measurement.

statement: Stellar kinematics can constrain Galactic mass models and dark matter, but this repository only audits radial-velocity measurement consistency and performs no dynamical dark-matter inference.
limitations: Better-calibrated velocities are an input to future dynamical studies, not a dark-matter result by themselves.

statement: The DESI stellar catalogue reports line-of-sight radial velocities fitted from spectra, including single-epoch measurements that make repeat-observation consistency tests possible.
limitations: Radial velocity is one component of motion and is not a star's full three-dimensional velocity.

statement: DESI's focal plane has ten PETAL wedges, each associated with 500 fibers and one spectrograph; PETAL is an instrumental location label, not a stellar property.
limitations: Association with PETAL does not uniquely locate a causal fault within the instrument or separate instrument geometry from correlated target assignment.

statement: After the published BACKUP correction and adopted uncertainty floors, a source-disjoint PROGRAM:NIGHT model reduces holdout raw robust scatter by 0.494756 km/s (13.55%), more than every one of 100 shuffled-night controls.
limitations: The offsets are relative diagnostics for known nights, not an official catalogue correction or a causal diagnosis.

statement: Two disjoint source halves recover 483 common PROGRAM:NIGHT offsets with Pearson correlation 0.98026 and slope 1.00157.
limitations: Split-half reproducibility reduces shared-source leakage concerns but both halves retain the same release, time span, nights, and observation-linked systematics.
The split does not identify the physical cause of the offsets.

statement: Successive supported BRIGHT and DARK nights separated by 1 to 7 days show program-conditioned persistence in their diagnostic offsets, with Pearson correlations 0.33759 and 0.61162 and full-pipeline maxT p=0.009901.
limitations: The statistic uses successive supported nights with 1-to-7-day gaps, not every possible pair of nights in that range.
Temporal persistence is compatible with multi-day states but does not prove instrument drift or identify a mechanism.

statement: The apparent same-night BRIGHT-DARK coherence does not reproduce after within-program graph separation and source-disjoint cross-comparison; the symmetric same-night correlation is 0.01003 with Holm-adjusted p=0.4614.
limitations: A null result under this design does not prove that no common component exists under every model or scale.

statement: A source-disjoint PETAL-associated residual remains beyond PROGRAM:NIGHT, with mean incremental gain 0.058141 km/s, 5 of 5 positive folds, source-half r=0.83133, and empirical p=0.01 from 99 controls.
limitations: PETAL association is not proof of a hardware fault and the model does not separate static PROGRAM:PETAL structure from genuinely night-varying structure.

statement: The constant-RV outlier lists are screening candidates, not confirmed variable stars or binaries, and they are not evidence for the PROGRAM:NIGHT result.
limitations: Confirmation needs source-specific astrophysical review and independent observations.

statement: The audit and discovery experiments are exploratory within DESI DR1; strong confirmation requires a pre-specified untouched release, independent survey, data slice, or unseen-night prediction test.
limitations: Frozen gates and source-disjoint evaluation improve credibility but do not turn the reused DR1 sample into untouched confirmatory data.
